lessons.c:
TwinCAT turns a standard Windows PC or Beckhoff industrial PC into a real-time controller. It runs PLC, motion and other modules in one real-time runtime.

Its PLC follows the IEC 61131-3 standard, and it talks to I/O mainly over EtherCAT.
lessons.x: One industrial PC runs the conveyor logic and the servo motion together, in sync over EtherCAT.
lessons.ex: Find the Beckhoff TwinCAT product page and list two functions besides PLC.
q: Software that turns a PC into a real-time controller
TwinCAT is Beckhoff’s PC-based control software.
Motion is a core TwinCAT function.
EtherCAT connects Beckhoff I/O and drives.
Predictable timing is what makes it real-time.

lessons.c:
The TwinCAT 3 engineering environment is called XAE (eXtended Automation Engineering) and is built on Microsoft Visual Studio.

The Solution Explorer shows a tree with SYSTEM, MOTION, PLC, SAFETY, C++ and I/O. PLC code lives under PLC, and hardware devices under I/O.
lessons.x: You add an EtherCAT device under I/O, then link its input terminal to a PLC variable.
lessons.ex: Open XAE, expand every tree node and write what you think each one is for.
q: Code for the PLC is written under:
The PLC node holds PLC projects.
The I/O node holds fieldbus devices and terminals.
TwinCAT 3 uses Visual Studio as its shell.
It is the tree of the whole project.

lessons.c:
In XAE create a new TwinCAT XAE project, then right-click PLC and add a new PLC project. It creates a POUs folder with a MAIN program and a task that calls MAIN every cycle.

POU means Program Organization Unit: a program, function or function block.
lessons.x: MAIN is the entry point of your machine program, called again and again by the task.
lessons.ex: Create a PLC project named FirstMachine and build it with no errors.
q: The task calls MAIN each cycle.
A POU is a program, function or function block.
A new PLC project is added under:
Run the PLC program cycle after cycle

lessons.c:
The runtime (XAR) executes your PLC on the target device. You choose the target system, activate the configuration, then log in to the PLC and start it.

The PLC task has a cycle time, such as 10 ms, and a priority.
lessons.x: A 10 ms cycle time means MAIN runs 100 times a second.
lessons.ex: Set a task cycle time of 10 ms and work out how many scans happen per second.
q: XAR is the eXtended Automation Runtime.
A 10 ms cycle time gives how many runs per second?
Connects to the running PLC on the target
Login connects you to monitor and control it.
Sends the configuration to the target
It loads your settings onto the target.
The runtime must be running to:
The PLC only executes while the runtime runs it.
